help:
rup: the command line of roundup

roundup runs coding Agents in a Project and shows the user their Status, Todos, Pads, Messages and Terminals. rup is how an Agent reads and changes all of that from its shell: every command acts as you, the Agent whose id is in ROUNDUP_AGENT.

Human-readable command output names Agents by Rail name. IDs remain command arguments and machine fields in --json.

Examples:
  rup pad read notes
  rup terminal read 3 --after 120
  rup todo create "Fix login"
  rup pad write notes - < notes.md

Commands:

  terminal
    rup terminal open [--cols <cols>] [--rows <rows>] [--workstream <workstream>]
        Start a login shell in a Terminal owned by a Workstream that is yours or in your Reach; `workstream` is required for Agents.
    rup terminal spawn <cwd> <cols> <rows> [--command <command>]... --env <env>
        Start a program in a Terminal owned by you; the answer holds its `id`.
    rup terminal close <id>
        Stop a Terminal you or your Reach own and forget it.
    rup terminal write <id> [<text>] [--no-enter] [--base64 <base64>]
        Type text into a Terminal you or your Reach own, then press Enter.
    rup terminal resize <id> <cols> <rows>
        Resize a Terminal you or your Reach own to `cols` by `rows`.
    rup terminal kill <id>
        Stop the program of a Terminal you or your Reach own.
    rup terminal show <id>
        Show a Terminal in your Reach to the user, who sees its owner selected. [Door only]
    rup terminal screen <id>
        Read a Terminal's screen as it is now, as plain text, with the `offset` to read from next.
    rup terminal read <id> [--after <after>] [--max <max>]
        Read a Terminal's output you have not read yet, as plain text; `next` is the offset after it.
    rup terminal search <id> <pattern> [--after <after>] [--max <max>]
        Search a Terminal's output for a regular expression and get the matching lines with their offsets.

  agent
    rup agent spawn <cwd> [--visibility <shown>] [--cols <cols>] [--rows <rows>] [--engine <engine>] [--prompt <prompt>] [--parent <parent>] [--order <order>] [--name <name>] [--model <model>] [--scout] [--specialist <specialist>] [--extras <extras>]
        Start a child Agent in a folder of this Project.
    rup agent extras
        List the skills, plugins and MCP servers of the user's setup that `agent_spawn`'s `extras` and `agent_extras_add` accept. [Door only]
    rup agent extras-add <id> --extras <extras>
        Give a running child of yours skills, plugins or MCP servers by name. [Door only]
    rup agent stop <id>
        Stop an Agent in your Reach, never yourself.
    rup agent prompt <id> <text>
        Send a prompt to an Agent in your Reach as the user would.
    rup agent interrupt <id>
        Interrupt the turn of an Agent in your Reach.
    rup agent worktree-state <id>
        Read what a Worktree holds: its changes and whether it can land.
    rup agent land <id>
        Land the Worktree of an Agent in your Reach on the Base branch.
    rup agent discard <id>
        Discard the Worktree of an Agent in your Reach and its changes.
    rup agent set-order [--captured <captured>] --order <order>
        Replace your own order: a Work order once the ask is clear, or a Clarification order while a question is open.
    rup agent set-visibility <id> <visibility>
        Choose shown or internal for a direct child. [Door only]
    rup agent instructions <id>
        Read exact instruction revisions and Attempt-bound delivery facts for yourself or an Agent in your Reach.
    rup agent run [--cols <cols>] [--rows <rows>] [--cwd <cwd>] --command <command>...
        Run a command in a Terminal of your own that the user can watch, in your Worktree or in `cwd`.
    rup agent resume <id> [--mode <normal>]
        Continue a saved conversation in your Reach.
    rup agent context
        Ask where you stand now: whom you report to, whom to ask, your peers, your open Todos and the Models you may start a child on.
    rup agent digest
        Ask what each of your direct children did: its Kind, its last line, its open Todos and the Pads it wrote since you were last told. [Door only]
    rup agent wake <id>... [--any]
        Ask to be woken when all, or with `any` the first, of the named Agents finish (idle, done, error or needs-you).

  rail
    rup rail tree
        Read the Rail: every Group, Workstream and Agent in tree order, with each Agent Status.
    rup rail create-workstream <name> [--parent <parent>] [--order <order>]
        Make a Workstream at the Project root or in a Group.
    rup rail move <id> <index> [--parent <parent>]
        Move a node in your Reach.
    rup rail rename <id> <name>
        Rename yourself or a node in your Reach.
    rup rail start-door <id>
        Start the Door of a Workstream you made, or of one in your Reach.
    rup rail remove <id> [--scope <this>] [--operation <operation>]
        Remove a node in your Reach, never yourself.

  project
    rup project set-worktrees --on [--check <check>]
        Turn Worktrees on or off for the Project and set the command Landing runs.
    rup project get
        Read the Project's settings.
    rup project rename <name>
        Ask the App to give this Project a name of 1 to 40 characters.
    rup project open <path>
        Open an absolute existing folder through the App.
    rup project start <path> --kind <agent> --name <name> --prompt <prompt>
        Start an Agent, Workstream or Mode with a prompt in a target Project through the App.

  import
    rup import list <period>
        Read-only: list this Project's saved and live top-level Claude Code sessions active in the period, once each, with the revision to approve.

  todo
    rup todo create <title> [--body <body>] [--blockers <blockers>]... [--owner <owner>] [--priority <low>]
        Create a Todo.
    rup todo get <id>
        Read one Todo.
    rup todo list
        List every Todo.
    rup todo update <id> [--title <title>] [--body <body>] [--priority <low>] [--expected-change <expected_change>]
        Change a Todo's title, body or priority.
    rup todo complete <id>
        Mark a Todo done.
    rup todo reopen <id>
        Reopen a done Todo.
    rup todo set-blockers <id> --blockers <blockers>... [--expected-change <expected_change>]
        Replace a Todo's whole blocker list.
    rup todo assign <id> [--owner <owner>] [--expected-change <expected_change>]
        Assign a Todo to an owner, or leave it unassigned.
    rup todo move <id> [--home <home>]
        Move a Todo into a Workstream, or out of every Workstream with a null `home`.
    rup todo reorder <id> [--before <before>]
        Put a Todo before another in the Todo order, or last with a null `before`.
    rup todo delete <operation> --ids <ids>...
        Delete exactly the chosen Todo ids.
    rup todo comment <id> <body>
        Leave a comment on a Todo only when the user must read it, such as a question or a blocker.
    rup todo comments <id>
        Read a Todo comment thread oldest first, including authors and user replies.
    rup todo ref add <id> <url>
        Point the user to a Pad or one section of it from a Todo, so they open it from the Todo and read it.
    rup todo ref remove <id> <url>
        Remove a Pad or Pad-section link from a Todo, by the same link you added; removing one the Todo lacks changes nothing.

  pad
    rup pad create <name> [--text <text>]
        Create a shared Pad.
    rup pad read <name>
        Read one Pad.
    rup pad list
        List every Pad.
    rup pad rename <name> <new-name> <expected-incarnation>
        Rename any Pad, keeping its creation and text.
    rup pad write <name> <text> [--expected-revision <expectedRevision>] [--expected-incarnation <expectedIncarnation>]
        Rewrite a Pad's whole text.
    rup pad append <name> <text>
        Add text to the end of any Pad.
    rup pad append-section <name> <heading> <text> [--expected-revision <expectedRevision>]
        Add text at the end of the section under a Markdown heading of any Pad; the heading ignores case and extra whitespace.
    rup pad move <name> [--home <home>]
        Move a Pad to a Workstream or the Project root.
    rup pad delete <name> [--operation <operation>] [--expected-incarnation <expectedIncarnation>]
        Delete a Pad, retaining its original creation for restoration.
    rup pad redo-delete <project> <restored-operation> <operation> <expected-incarnation> <expected-revision> [--expected-home <expectedHome>]
        Redo a restored Pad deletion with an acknowledged creation, Revision and Home; retain the current authoritative state for Undo.
    rup pad get-deletion <operation>
        Reconcile an unknown Pad deletion on its originating Project.
    rup pad restore <project> <operation>
        Restore your retained Pad deletion once, without replaying external effects.
    rup pad export <name> <path>
        Write a Pad's text to a file at an absolute path.
    rup pad set-storage --files
        Choose whether the Project mirrors its Pads to files.

  message
    rup message send <to> <kind> <body> [--reply-to <replyTo>]
        Send a note or a question to an Agent or the user.
    rup message get <id>
        Read one Message you sent or received.
    rup message list [--to <to>] [--id <id>] [--status <pending>]
        List the Messages you sent or received, newest last.
    rup message progress <project> <id>
        Inspect retained instructions, reports, acceptance and declared verification without starting work.
    rup message report <project> <id> <key> <delivery> <result> <next> --target <target> --output <output> --state <state> --check <check>
        Report your own Attempt's result for an exact delivered instruction and published output.
    rup message accept-result <project> <id> <report> <evidence>
        Record user acceptance of one exact reported result with its evidence; only the user may accept.
    rup message verify-result <project> <id> <report>
        Observe a report's declared authoritative condition without a Model call; unavailable or unsupported evidence stays unknown.
    rup message resolve-result <project> <id> <report> <source>
        User only: authorize a read-only authoritative receipt source for an unknown external effect.
    rup message reconcile-work <project> <id>
        Read which retained work is unfinished, confirmed, pending a check or uncertain, without sending or starting anything.
    rup message resume-work <project> <id> <request> [--action <action>]
        User only: resume an Agent's eligible unfinished work with one successor Message.

  route
    rup route set <from> <to> <delivery>
        Set where one Agent's Messages to another go: `auto` or `drop`.
    rup route list
        List the Routes: who each Agent's questions go to.

  deliverable
    rup deliverable publish <key> <title> --target <target>
        Deliberately publish a file, expected Pad incarnation and Revision or current external URL.
    rup deliverable list [--home <home>] [--maker <maker>]
        List published results without reading retained payloads.
    rup deliverable get <project> <id>
        Read publication metadata by its Project and identity.
    rup deliverable resolve <project> <id>
        Resolve the recorded revision or exact current external target, or its unavailability cause.
    rup deliverable move <project> <id> [--home <home>]
        Move a published result; an Agent cannot override user placement.
    rup deliverable remove <project> <id>
        Explicitly remove a publication.

  github
    rup github pr-get <number>
        Read a PR of the Project's repository as GitHub holds it now: title, body, state, draft, autoMerge, head and mergedAt. [Door only]
    rup github issue-get <number>
        Read an Issue of the Project's repository as GitHub holds it now: title, body, state, labels and stateReason. [Door only]
    rup github pr-set-body <number> <body>
        Replace a PR's body with `body` (not empty); the answer is the PR as it now stands. [Door only]
    rup github pr-ready <number>
        Mark a draft PR ready for review; a PR already ready is left as it is. [Door only]
    rup github pr-auto-merge <number>
        Enable auto-merge (merge commit) on an open PR; one already enabled is left as it is. [Door only]

  api
    rup api list [--quiet]
        List every method the Daemon serves with a one-line summary.
    rup api describe <method>
        Describe one method: its summary, params and result schemas and an example.

  link
    rup link read <url>
        Read a Project roundup:// link: current Pad, Todo, Agent, Workstream or Terminal content, or a Deliverable recorded revision/current external target and its availability.

  provenance
    rup provenance history <item>
        List the Touches on one item, such as `todo:3` or `rail:5`.
    rup provenance touched <actor-id>
        List the Touches one Actor made.

  workstream
    rup workstream rewind --turns <turns>...
        Ask each named child's provider to rewind it through the provider's own feature: Claude Code restores the child's files to the state at the user message `turn` of its conversation. [Door only]

  streams
    rup events [--after <after>] [--kept] [--follow]
        Print the Events saved after a number, one JSON object per line, then stop at the end of the log.
        Example: rup events --after 12 --follow --json

  actions
    rup actions [--json]
        List the App's named actions.
        Example: rup actions
    rup do <name> [key=value]...
        Run a named action of the App.
        Example: rup do agent.new-with-prompt prompt="Fix login"

  other
    rup help [<command>]
        Print this help, or a command's.
    rup ping
        Check the Daemon answers.
    rup mcp <agent-id>
        Serve these commands as MCP tools over stdio.
    rup signal <agent-id>
        Hook: hand the Daemon a Signal from stdin.
    rup context <agent-id>
        Hook: print the Agent's Context.
    rup skill <setup|status|remove>
        Teach other Claude Code sessions about roundup.

Options of every command:
    --agent <id>   Act as this Agent instead of ROUNDUP_AGENT
    --json         Print the result as JSON on stdout
    -h, --help     Print a command's arguments, flags and an example

A text argument takes `-` to read the whole of stdin, so a long body is never quoted.
`rup help <noun>` lists a noun's commands; `rup help <noun> <verb>` describes one.

Exit codes:
    0  done
    1  failed: the Daemon refused, did not answer within 10 s, or was not there
    2  bad usage: an unknown command, a missing or invalid argument, no Agent id, a Door-only command run by an Agent

rup drives rupd, the roundup Daemon, from a shell or an MCP client.

usage: rup [--as ext:<name>] [--json] <command>

commands, and who may run each (User: a shell outside every Agent; Ext: --as ext:<name>):
  ping        show which Daemon answered
              User: yes   Ext: yes
  mcp         serve the roundup tools over MCP on stdio (rup mcp <agent-id> for an Agent)
              User: yes   Ext: yes
  signal      an Agent's hook (rup signal <agent-id>)
              User: no    Ext: no
  context     an Agent's hook (rup context <agent-id>)
              User: no    Ext: no
  help        print this text

options, before the command:
  --as ext:<name>  act as the Ext Actor ext:<name> (1 to 64 of a-z 0-9 - _), so calls are Touches under that name
  --json           with ping, print {actor, socket, result}, who rup acted as included

RUPD_SOCKET names the Daemon's socket; unset, rup uses ~/.roundup/rupd.sock.
`rup ping` shows which Daemon answered.

gh api --help.stdout:
Makes an authenticated HTTP request to the GitHub API and prints the response.

The endpoint argument should either be a path of a GitHub API v3 endpoint, or
`graphql` to access the GitHub API v4.

Placeholder values `{owner}`, `{repo}`, and `{branch}` in the endpoint
argument will get replaced with values from the repository of the current
directory or the repository specified in the `GH_REPO` environment variable.
Note that in some shells, for example PowerShell, you may need to enclose
any value that contains `{...}` in quotes to prevent the shell from
applying special meaning to curly braces.

The `-p/--preview` flag enables opting into previews, which are feature-flagged,
experimental API endpoints or behaviors. The API expects opt-in via the `Accept`
header with format `application/vnd.github.<preview-name>-preview+json` and this
command facilitates that via `--preview <preview-name>`. To send a request for
the corsair and scarlet witch previews, you could use `-p corsair,scarlet-witch`
or `--preview corsair --preview scarlet-witch`.

The default HTTP request method is `GET` normally and `POST` if any parameters
were added. Override the method with `--method`.

Pass one or more `-f/--raw-field` values in `key=value` format to add static string
parameters to the request payload. To add non-string or placeholder-determined values, see
`-F/--field` below. Note that adding request parameters will automatically switch the
request method to `POST`. To send the parameters as a `GET` query string instead, use
`--method GET`.

The `-F/--field` flag has magic type conversion based on the format of the value:

- literal values `true`, `false`, `null`, and integer numbers get converted to
  appropriate JSON types;
- placeholder values `{owner}`, `{repo}`, and `{branch}` get populated with values
  from the repository of the current directory;
- if the value starts with `@`, the rest of the value is interpreted as a
  filename to read the value from. Pass `-` to read from standard input.

For GraphQL requests, all fields other than `query` and `operationName` are
interpreted as GraphQL variables.

To pass nested parameters in the request payload, use `key[subkey]=value` syntax when
declaring fields. To pass nested values as arrays, declare multiple fields with the
syntax `key[]=value1`, `key[]=value2`. To pass an empty array, use `key[]` without a
value.

To pass pre-constructed JSON or payloads in other formats, a request body may be read
from file specified by `--input`. Use `-` to read from standard input. When passing the
request body this way, any parameters specified via field flags are added to the query
string of the endpoint URL.

In `--paginate` mode, all pages of results will sequentially be requested until
there are no more pages of results. For GraphQL requests, this requires that the
original query accepts an `$endCursor: String` variable and that it fetches the
`pageInfo{ hasNextPage, endCursor }` set of fields from a collection. Each page is a separate
JSON array or object. Pass `--slurp` to wrap all pages of JSON arrays or objects
into an outer JSON array.

For more information about output formatting flags, see `gh help formatting`.

USAGE
  gh api <endpoint> [flags]

FLAGS
      --allow-escape-sequences   Allow printing terminal escape sequences
      --cache duration           Cache the response, e.g. "3600s", "60m", "1h"
  -F, --field key=value          Add a typed parameter in key=value format (use "@<path>" or "@-" to read value from file or stdin)
  -H, --header key:value         Add a HTTP request header in key:value format
      --hostname string          The GitHub hostname for the request (default "github.com")
  -i, --include                  Include HTTP response status line and headers in the output
      --input file               The file to use as body for the HTTP request (use "-" to read from standard input)
  -q, --jq string                Query to select values from the response using jq syntax
  -X, --method string            The HTTP method for the request (default "GET")
      --paginate                 Make additional HTTP requests to fetch all pages of results
  -p, --preview strings          Opt into GitHub API previews (names should omit '-preview')
  -f, --raw-field key=value      Add a string parameter in key=value format
      --silent                   Do not print the response body
      --slurp                    Use with "--paginate" to return an array of all pages of either JSON arrays or objects
  -t, --template string          Format JSON output using a Go template; see "gh help formatting"
      --verbose                  Include full HTTP request and response in the output

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help   Show help for command

EXAMPLES
  # List releases in the current repository
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases
  
  # Post an issue comment
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/123/comments -f body='Hi from CLI'
  
  # Post nested parameter read from a file
  $ gh api gists -F 'files[myfile.txt][content]=@myfile.txt'
  
  # Add parameters to a GET request
  $ gh api -X GET search/issues -f q='repo:cli/cli is:open remote'
  
  # Use a JSON file as request body
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets --input file.json
  
  # Set a custom HTTP header
  $ gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.v3.raw+json' ...
  
  # Opt into GitHub API previews
  $ gh api --preview baptiste,nebula ...
  
  # Print only specific fields from the response
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues --jq '.[].title'
  
  # Use a template for the output
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues --template \
    '{{range .}}{{.title}} ({{.labels | pluck "name" | join ", " | color "yellow"}}){{"\n"}}{{end}}'
  
  # Update allowed values of the "environment" custom property in a deeply nested array
  $ gh api -X PATCH /orgs/{org}/properties/schema \
     -F 'properties[][property_name]=environment' \
     -F 'properties[][default_value]=production' \
     -F 'properties[][allowed_values][]=staging' \
     -F 'properties[][allowed_values][]=production'
  
  # List releases with GraphQL
  $ gh api graphql -F owner='{owner}' -F name='{repo}' -f query='
    query($name: String!, $owner: String!) {
      repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {
        releases(last: 3) {
          nodes { tagName }
        }
      }
    }
  '
  
  # List all repositories for a user
  $ gh api graphql --paginate -f query='
    query($endCursor: String) {
      viewer {
        repositories(first: 100, after: $endCursor) {
          nodes { nameWithOwner }
          pageInfo {
            hasNextPage
            endCursor
          }
        }
      }
    }
  '
  
  # Get the percentage of forks for the current user
  $ gh api graphql --paginate --slurp -f query='
    query($endCursor: String) {
      viewer {
        repositories(first: 100, after: $endCursor) {
          nodes { isFork }
          pageInfo {
            hasNextPage
            endCursor
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ' | jq 'def count(e): reduce e as $_ (0;.+1);
  [.[].data.viewer.repositories.nodes[]] as $r | count(select($r[].isFork))/count($r[])'

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
  GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN (in order of precedence): an authentication token for
  `github.com` API requests.
  
  GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN (in order of precedence): an
  authentication token for API requests to GitHub Enterprise.
  
  GH_HOST: make the request to a GitHub host other than `github.com`.

LEARN MORE
  Use `gh <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual
  Learn about exit codes using `gh help exit-codes`
  Learn about accessibility experiences using `gh help accessibility`

2214.body:
The owner: "does "rup --help"? if not it should also "rup help". Treat rup as the product your work agents see. An agent should learn it from rup help alone", then: "The CLI guidelines at clig.dev: help, --json output, stable exit codes". Asked to pick, the owner chose: every MCP tool also becomes a rup command.

What it does today (`crates/rup/src/main.rs`):
- `rup --help`, `rup -h` and `rup help` print `rup: unknown command "--help"` and exit 2.
- Bare `rup` prints one usage line to stderr and exits 2.
- rup has 5 commands (ping, signal, context, permission, mcp). The 62 tools `rup mcp` offers every Agent (65 for a Door) are reachable only over MCP.

Wanted, following https://clig.dev:
- **One list, two faces.** Every tool `rup mcp` offers is also a command: `rup <noun> <verb>` for method `noun.verb` (`rup pad read notes`, `rup terminal read 3 --after 120`, `rup todo create "Fix login"`). Flags and arguments come from the tool's own schema, and the help text from its description. Both faces read the same list, so a tool can never exist on one and not the other; a test fails if they differ.
- **Help.** `rup`, `rup help`, `rup -h` and `rup --help` print the help to stdout and exit 0. It says what roundup and rup are, shows a few examples first, then the commands grouped by noun, then the exit codes. `rup help <command>` and `rup <command> --help` show that command's arguments, flags and an example. An agent that reads only `rup help` can use every command.
- **Output.** Plain text by default, the same text the MCP tool returns. `--json` prints the method's result as JSON on stdout. Errors go to stderr with what to do next; a mistyped command suggests the closest one.
- **Stable exit codes**, listed in the help: 0 done, 1 failed (the Daemon refused or did not answer), 2 bad usage. The hook commands `signal`, `context` and `permission` never exit 2, since exit 2 makes Claude Code block the tool call or prompt; their usage errors stay at 1.
- **Who is asking.** A command that acts as an Agent uses the Agent id roundup gives that Agent's shell, or `--agent <id>`; with neither it says so and exits 2. A Door gets the Door-only commands, as over MCP.
- **Speed.** `rup signal`, `rup context` and `rup permission` stay inside their hook deadlines (1 s and 4 s); measure startup before and after.
- **Text in, not base64.** The owner: "Our CLI must have full parity with the MCP", and their work agents drive roundup through `rup` alone. `rup terminal write <id> "text"` types plain text and presses Enter, as Solo's `send_input` does (1923 of the owner's Solo calls); `--no-enter` leaves Enter out and `--base64` sends the raw bytes `terminal_write` takes. `rup agent prompt <id> "text"` does the same for an Agent.
- **Long text from stdin or a file.** Any text argument (`pad write`, `pad append`, `message send`, `agent spawn --order`, `agent spawn --prompt`) also takes `-` for stdin, so an Agent never quotes a long body in the shell.
- **Same limits and plain output.** `rup terminal read` prints the text and the `next` offset on stderr or in `--json`, so a loop of reads needs no parsing; the 16 384-byte cap and the 10 s call timeout stay as over MCP.
- The Agent's Brief tells it to run `rup help` to learn roundup.
- `rup mcp` keeps working unchanged.

Reuse: a maintained argument parser (for example clap, bpaf, argh) over hand-written matching.

## Outcome
Every App command has a stable name and arguments. The menu bar, the Switcher, the keys and the `rup` CLI all run commands from that one list, and `rup actions` lists it and `rup do <name>` runs one.

## Outside evidence
Outside evidence: the owner studied Rex, Superlogical's Mac terminal multiplexer, and its docs (https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/llms-full.txt). In Rex each action has a name and `key=value` arguments; the command palette, keybindings and the CLI run the same actions; `rex actions` lists them and `rex do <name> key=value` runs one, failing on an unknown argument.

## Scope
Start from X2 (#3787, U3787b): the menu already covers every bound chord and runs one shared action per chord (#4308). Specify the lesson for its three implementation Issues, in order: stable names and arguments for each `CHORDS` and `LEADER` entry in `apps/desktop` (`keys/chords.ts`, `keys/registry.ts`); the Daemon relay that lets a caller list and run the App's actions in `crates/rupd` (Contract recipe); and `rup actions` and `rup do <name> [key=value…]` in `crates/rup`. Name the terms in `GLOSSARY.md`.

This is a specification run. Write the acceptance for the whole lesson in `scenarios/named-actions.md` as bounded given/when/then scenarios, each with a named observer. Then edit each Issue this one blocks so its `Scenarios:` line names its IDs, and close this Issue from the specification PR. Change no product code.

## Regression requirements
U3787b: menu and key run one identical action once against the same target and never take editor or Terminal input. U2241: no new App-scope chord. `rup do` with the App closed fails with a cause and fix. Every action `rup do` runs keeps its existing confirm and undo rules.

Source: the owner accepted this Rex UX lesson (4) on 2026-10-31.

5251.body:
## Outcome
The owner runs `rup skill setup`, or turns it on in Settings, and a Claude Code they start outside roundup learns the `rup` commands and reports its state to roundup. `rup skill status` shows what is installed; `rup skill remove` takes out only what roundup installed; `--dry-run` shows changes without making them.

## Outside evidence
Outside evidence: the owner studied Rex, Superlogical's Mac terminal multiplexer, and its docs (https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/llms-full.txt). `rex skill setup` finds installed agents and installs a skill (`~/.claude/skills/rex`) that teaches the `rex` commands and reads its guide from the installed `rex`, plus a session-start hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` that tells the agent where it runs. It leaves the rest of the settings file as it was, reports `unchanged` on a rerun, follows `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and refuses to replace a skill of that name it did not install without `--force`. `rex skill status` reports `current`, `outdated`, `missing`, `foreign`, `unreadable` or `unsupported` per item; `rex skill remove` removes only what Rex installed.

## Scope
Specify the lesson for three implementation Issues, in order: the Claude Code installer in `crates/agents` (`src/claude_code/`, since P4 keeps vendor paths there), the `rup skill` commands in `crates/rup`, and the Settings toggle in `apps/desktop`. Decide how the hook reports state; the program status lesson (OSC 7501) is the proposed path.

This is a specification run. Write the acceptance for the whole lesson in `scenarios/skill-setup.md` as bounded given/when/then scenarios, each with a named observer. Then edit each Issue this one blocks so its `Scenarios:` line names its IDs, and close this Issue from the specification PR. Change no product code.

## Regression requirements
P4: roundup extends the user's settings, never replaces or hides them; vendor strings stay in `crates/agents/<vendor>/`. P9: nothing changes the settings file of a running roundup Agent's session. Agents roundup starts keep their Brief and hooks.

Source: the owner accepted this Rex UX lesson (13) on 2026-10-31.
